daily_reality.typical_workday: 8-9 hour days (9AM-5PM typical) in clinics or private practice. 70-80% of day on direct patient care. Morning: patient assessments using audiometers, tympanometry, otoacoustic emissions (OAE), balance evaluations, newborn screenings. Midday: fitting, programming, and verifying hearing aids, cochlear implants, and assistive devices. Patient counseling on hearing loss prevention, device maintenance, and lifestyle adjustments. Collaboration with ENT specialists, SLPs, and primary care providers. Specialized duties: workplace hearing tests for OSHA compliance. Afternoon: professional development, administrative work, next-day preparation.
deadlines: AuD clinical experience hours (1,820 hours including 375 post-graduate)
Hearing aid warranty and return periods
daily_reality.seasonality: Back-to-school hearing screenings peak in August-September. Newborn screening year-round. Holiday season increases hearing aid purchases (gifts). Better Hearing and Speech Month (May) drives awareness and appointments. Year-round demand from aging population. OSHA workplace testing follows annual compliance schedules.

laws: State audiology practice acts (all 50 states regulate)
regulatory.licensing: AuD (Doctor of Audiology) — 7-8 years total education. Pass Praxis exam. State licensure in all 50 states. CCC-A (ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence) — voluntary but widely expected. 1,820 supervised clinical hours required. ASLP Interstate Compact: 37 jurisdictions as of November 2025 — CompactConnect launched September 2025. Nevada (July 2025) and Ohio onboarding into 2026. ABA (American Board of Audiology) certification also available.
regulatory.penalties: State board penalties: fines, probation, suspension, revocation for practice violations. Practicing without license carries state-specific penalties. OSHA non-compliance penalties for workplace hearing programs. Hearing aid dispensing violations. Medicare fraud penalties for improper billing.

career_psychology.burnout: No extensive audiologist-specific burnout data in literature. Common allied health concerns apply: high patient loads, administrative demands, insurance authorization frustrations, and emotional aspects of working with hearing loss patients. OTC hearing aid disruption creating professional identity anxiety. ASHA offers mental health support resources for members.
